Day Two artwork and game sequence review

This first pass gives the owner a library for reviewing each image and deciding what to refine next. It covers the fifteen implemented career families, the active Opera practice and stage variants, all eight existing birthday job adapters, the optional Arborist Tree Book practice, the owner-directed birthday replacement gap and newly published final-act contest plans. The clearest strengths are the cake progression, rainbow candle, isolated tools, shape-coded candy and much of the Tree Book art. The largest weaknesses are inconsistent cutouts, schematic overlays, unclear subject ownership and the difference between polished source pictures and a convincing played sequence.

The illustrated library displays all 637 source images, with an individual score, observation, refinement action, usage qualification, dimensions, original source link and SHA-256. 432 images score at or below 4.5/5, including exactly 4.5. This is the owner's requested inclusive refinement threshold. The priority queue can be sorted independently. The library also contains 40 current or planned contexts, 190 phase or beat evaluations and 23 earlier composition captures (105 implemented phase evaluations and 85 proposed contest/option beats). These counts describe review coverage, not accepted gameplay.

What the scores mean

The source score is a first-pass Codex design opinion about the visible image: recognizable identity, painted finish, contour and cutout quality, broad value/color hierarchy, and clarity of its stated visual role. It is deliberately separate from a provisional game design/sequence score. Neither score is a canonical runtime grade. Motion, contact, current composed-runtime quality, device behavior and owner acceptance remain ungraded where they have not been observed.

Scores from 4.6 to 4.9 identify strong reuse candidates. Scores from 4.0 to 4.5 identify useful art with a specific refinement or context dependency. Scores from 3.0 to 3.9 indicate inconsistent finish, ambiguous ownership or a substantial source/composition issue. Scores below 3.0 identify a large visible presentation problem. A 5/5 requires owner acceptance in runtime under DL-VIS-07; this pass awards no 5s. There is no global average claiming compliance under DL-VIS-08.

Every file was inspected in source contact sheets, including raster previews of the five SVGs. Repeated family observations are preserved in individual records rather than pretending that a shared style issue is unique to every tile or costume pose. This is a breadth-first review; native-size edge inspection is a follow-up action where specified. Atlas previews display the complete sheets, including all cells. A sheet score does not certify every cell as an animation frame or assign a played-motion score.

The baseline is 55032e88936b22723fd9af5282c61ba6696b3d43, freshly fetched from origin/dev. The initial artwork/runtime baseline is preserved in review history; one relevant source update, Rumi’s native transparency repair, is re-reviewed from integration 08acb0ce529660e79de6784aa4124352798bc4cd. Runtime code remains unchanged; the September 30 target contest authority and per-pose handoff are reconciled from integration revision 285355eb9e09a29aa4ac53d36874e31419d4674e. Production controller and domain-authority hashes are recorded in inventory.json. Source records live in reviews.json; context and phase evaluations live in evaluations.json. This audit authors no runtime, save or source-art edit and changes no finding acceptance state; it inherits the separately recorded Rumi repair during integration reconciliation. The evaluations were authored by Codex; no human or owner acceptance is claimed.

Which jobs currently exist

The production career tables register Chef, Detective, Ballerina, Candy Maker, Doctor, Farmer, Boxer, Magician, Painter, Astronaut, Racer, Nursery, Popstar, Geologist and Teacher. The active two-act plan is limited to Ballerina, Magician and Popstar. Each uses its first three phases in practice, then all its source phases on stage. Other careers have recommended practice counts in the plan, but those recommendations are not an implemented two-act rollout.

The existing birthday order is Farmer, Chef, Candy Maker, Painter, Ballerina, Popstar, Astronaut and Detective. Their adapters are reviewed as they are implemented. The September 29 owner direction changes the intended assignment: Candy Maker is reserved for later outside Kitchen, and Arborist should provide the Opera training and Sky Lagoon party-tree story. The optional single-patient Tree Book practice is implemented separately; it is not a registered sixteenth global career and does not complete the birthday replacement.

The design language retains a scoped thirteen-career shipping contract and earlier evidence. This review explicitly includes the additional current Geologist and Teacher source routes, without rewriting that contract or claiming their acceptance. Current authority comes from the design language, document ledger, master planning entry, and the applicable scoped domain documents.

First refinement priorities

  1. Resolve story and visual subject ownership. Follow the Arborist replacement direction; preserve legacy Candy completion credit and existing save keys. Verify that Painter changes the banner, Astronaut parks the rocket despite the shared push_racer context, and Detective reveals the unlit candle instead of a crown-era reward. These are distinct continuity checks, not a claim that the suspicious metadata is an observed rendered defect.
  2. Inspect the most obvious cutout/style outliers. The faceted racer portrait D2A-0054 scores 1.9. The bop puff D2A-0394, ballet flower disc D2A-0605, opaque spotlight D2A-0611 and older tail-cropped Roshan cards D2A-0259 through D2A-0261 have specific visible defects. Establish actual draw routes before spending on art that is inactive or bypassed.
  3. Integrate Tree Book specimens. D2A-0056 and D2A-0057 have opaque navy backing and denser rendering than the clean book/patient family. A separate isolation of the same existing artwork is the first candidate. Review spot contrast, four-choice size, medicine contact and same-patient healing before new art.
  4. Keep protected doll identities while reviewing their isolation. D2A-0621 and D2A-0622 retain cropped edges and neighboring/baseline remnants. Preserve the book originals. Any later authorized isolation must be saved separately with source attribution. This audit grants no permission to modify the protected files.
  5. Improve the composed action before expanding decorative art. Geologist's earlier captures are mostly flat tan diagrams. Teacher's simple shapes work well, but a large board dominates the library. Several other careers have generic rings, fills and zigzags that may be bypassed by current specialist drawing. Capture the current route and preserve good mechanics while improving local material change.
  6. Review whole background families together. Deep Detective values and dense Opera decoration need target/character contrast checks. Source padding is visible in many derivatives, but the runtime crop excludes part of it. A source border is not proof of a live border. A 2048 derivative is also not proof of 2048 native authored coverage per playable screen. Preserve joins and composition; do not independently regenerate individual tile objects.

The priority queue is a review queue, not a bulk regeneration order. Low-scoring retired base cards belong to the reference appendix; they should not be revived to satisfy this audit. Reuse strong existing isolated art, choose reviewed poses, fix staging, and make separate bounded derivatives where authorized. No new artwork was generated.

Opera careers and training sequences

Chef — provisional design score 4.2. Pitcher, whisk, toppings and cake are strong reusable art. The five phases should read as one material process: batter enters the bowl, stirring changes it, baking changes color, frosting settles on the cake, and toppings remain. The local action must be visible before a progress or result card. The birthday cake is a separate six-tier identity and must not be replaced by the smaller free-play cake.

Detective — 3.7. Magnifier, paw/feather/ribbon tokens and chest are coherent. The deep navy background and dark actor edges are the main hierarchy concern. Keep the lens reveal spatially bound to the clue, make the case-board tokens distinguishable without reading, and avoid an opaque spotlight plate. The free-play crown result is valid in its own route; the birthday candle is different.

Ballerina — 4.2. Pearl Mirror, Ribbon Trail and Grand Twirl repeat in practice and stage. Earlier captures show clear large pose choices and a visible Roshan, but the task spotlight and top progress card dominate the composition. Keep the pose vocabulary distinct and show a real deliberate dance/bow payoff. Cycling different atlas gestures or moving the whole portrait is not sufficient acting evidence.

Candy Maker — 4.0. The replacement full-bleed syrup workshop and flower/shell/wrapper candy trio are strong. Full/empty pitcher states support a truthful before/after. Review pouring contact, mold alignment, wrapper change and one candy delivered to one friend. The legacy wrapper mover has a remnant; the contextual renderer may bypass it. The free-play family remains useful for the later owner-intended Candy Maker context.

Doctor — 4.0. The star plush and scanner are excellent anchors. Keep one patient from FIND through X-RAY, CAST and BANDAGE. Washing should occur on the actual hands; the scanner should reveal the area directly underneath it; a bandage should accumulate around the patient. A spinning roll or abstract ring does not prove care. Current semantic work-pose selections are a mitigation, not acceptance of every atlas cell.

Farmer — 4.1. Seed, pigs, carrot, corn and pumpkin share readable rounded contours. Show the seed landing in soil, a vegetable meeting the pig, the herd crossing the actual gate and one picnic snack beside each pig. The group picnic image is attractive but has multiple ownership roles. Generic movement overlays cannot replace the local result.

Boxer — 4.2. Glove Guide, Jab Practice, Soft Guard, Title Imp and Belt form a coherent soft toy sport. The mitt and rounded rival are good sources. The critical visual evidence is glove-to-mitt contact, safe guard position, a readable opportunity star and calm recovery. Old charge/slash/defeated source poses are individually scored but are not presumed to be current mandatory phases.

Magician — 4.0. Vanish, Track and Rope are the practice subset; the stage adds Cabinet and Portal. Preserve established Lamba identity through the full sequence. Inspect hat tracking, rope material change and cabinet-door contact. The portal has heavy framing, while some older movers include whole platforms. Earlier captures show the approved white Lamba cutout; alternate reward lambs need identity comparison before reuse.

Painter — 4.1. The blank canvas and framed sunrise are strong. The opaque-backed brush and twin-easel platform alternatives are weaker sources. Verify the current brush reveals paint only under contact, stamps stay on the canvas, and the selected frame receives that same picture. For the birthday adapter, all three phases must instead preserve the actual banner and Main Hall placement.

Astronaut — 3.9. The toy rocket and gold valve are attractive, but flat patch/pipe symbols introduce a different finish. Keep the same rocket through routing, patching and valve work. Free-play LAUNCH is valid; the birthday route ends parked-ready and must remain unlaunched. A source inspection cannot prove the exact pipe/socket contact or final rocket movement.

Racer — 3.8. Track, wrench and trophy are strong. The faceted portrait is the clearest style outlier and the wheel is softer than neighboring art. Earlier captures show plausible racing, but do not resolve driver seating, fin ownership, wheel contact or two-lap gate emphasis. The static racer Roshan card is actively loaded by RacerSurface, so its staging deserves priority over unused fallback cards.

Nursery — 3.9. Pastel babies, bottle and mobile form a calm family. The flat cradle/pillow alternatives are weaker. Review the current specialist route for safe landing, one baby at a time, bottle-to-mouth contact, gentle burping and the same baby settling into bed. Faron should remain a cooperative visible partner. Source presence does not establish that an older basin overlay is drawn.

Popstar — 4.1. Sound Check, Dance and Rhythm form practice; the stage adds Encore. The mic and broad arrow pads are coherent. Earlier stage compositions contain competing music landmarks and task UI. Keep the singer and one active cue prominent. Generic neon charge/encore discs should not stand in for performance. Rumi is a separate birthday partner with a protected source sheet.

Geologist — 3.0. The earlier River, Fossil, Pan and Geode captures show clear mechanics but largely flat tan panels and diagram symbols. This is the weakest illustrated composition family in the reviewed historical examples. Retain intentional brushing/sifting/reveal mechanics while giving each real material and specimen the painted finish of stronger career props. Current captures are required before calling those historical weaknesses present in the latest build.

Teacher — 3.8. Pattern, Count, Add and Match use excellent simple circles, triangles and pearls. The earlier capture's large board and text header dominate the pleasant library. Preserve shape contrast and countable spacing; make voice and picture cues sufficient and develop a visible learning-circle relationship with Roshan. Simplifying the task graphics further would not address the composition issue.

Planned final act contests

The September 30 Opera imp contest specification arrived during this pass and is covered separately in the library. It specifies twelve contests using existing job skills: Chef topping race, Detective sparkle search, Ballerina twirl-off, Candy Maker sharing, Doctor bandaging, Farmer feeding, Boxer title bout, Magician hat duel, Painter paint-off, Astronaut repair/launch, Racer Grand Prix and Popstar sing-off. Nursery, Geologist and Teacher retain unresolved cooperative/competitive options. These future compositions receive pending graphics scores because they have not been built or rendered.

DL-INT-14 allows the imp to enter at the final act, win the job contest and trigger an immediate friendly rematch while earlier earned progress is preserved. The contest-only restart interpretation remains an existing owner question in that handoff. The picture sequence now needs an entrance, readable owned work at each station, a local flub, wordless progress, an imp-win/reset beat and a Roshan-win/flourish beat. The library evaluates each proposed beat, with explicit implementation and capture gaps. Birthday story and tutorial runs opt out.

The supporting handoff inventory maps all 178 imp source files to current source usage and proposed pose roles. Forty-one are selected by current source routes; the planned twelve contests would use 156, or 167 with the plain-imp Nursery option. Those are the handoff's source-route counts, not newly observed played-state counts. Each of the 178 individual review records now carries that exact source citation, baseline and planned role. The source file presence no longer implies that every pose is displayed today.

The key graphics risk is reuse selection. The written plan names several retired framed widget bases and static Roshan cards that crop her tail. Existing full-tail atlases and current borderless draw routes are better starting points. Reusing source artwork should not reintroduce rejected card framing. The suggested medicine overlay or new Nursery/Geologist/Teacher costumes remain optional gaps or owner-dependent proposals, not automatic generation orders. Each proposed imp action must have readable contact with its real job object; cycling a charge/slash pair beside a miniature picture is not sufficient.

Birthday jobs and cross job continuity

Farmer — 4.5. Current code creates five individual single-berry pickup buttons. The three-fruit cluster is not the active pickup texture. Inspect the basket's five-fruit state and delivery; push_farmer also has a pig-era mover, so verify the story renderer before claiming a wrong subject.

Chef — 4.5. This is the strongest authored state progression. The six baked tiers, stack, frosting and five-strawberry final cake retain one specific object. The STACK goal is three taps while the artwork has six tiers: inspect what the played sequence actually accounts for, rather than declaring a defect from the number alone. The same cake must arrive at the table with its base visibly supported.

Candy Maker — 3.5. This provisional sequence score reflects a current assignment that conflicts with the latest owner direction, plus uncertainty about meaningful strawberry sorting. It does not reduce the beautiful cake/pitcher source grades. Preserve the family for later, and migrate the birthday responsibility under the existing owner scope without deleting save keys or losing legacy completion credit.

Painter — 3.8. The rainbow banner and shell/star motifs are good sources. Verify the banner is what the brush reveals and stamps modify. The selected hanging point must contain the same completed banner after return. Sunrise-era Painter metadata and assets are a route-review dependency, not proof that the wrong picture is currently rendered.

Ballerina — 3.9. The playroom belongs to the story and the original cat/bunny identities must be retained. The nook is background decoration. The two active stuffies must independently mirror, twirl and bow beside Roshan; replayed ballet pearl/ribbon mechanics alone do not establish their acting payoff. Review cutout remnants without changing protected originals.

Popstar — 4.2. Production code loads Rumi's eight-pose runtime sheet. The incoming native repair restores the upright fins; source review retains 4.5/5 because fine green/white fringe and pose-scale variation remain. Review relative scale, gaze, microphone ownership, stage movement and the same-group encore. Do not infer sung performance or motion quality from a static identity sheet. Keep the three rhythm cues visually distinct and readable without text.

Astronaut — 3.6. The intended result is explicitly parked-ready and unlaunched. READY PARK names push_racer; verify the actual override/draw path in a current capture so the rocket remains the subject. The adapter's parked flag alone does not prove a visually correct result, and the shared context alone does not prove a kart defect.

Detective — 4.3. The unlit rainbow candle is an excellent specific final clue and a dedicated scene interaction exists. Review storybook clue identity and final visibility, and confirm crown-era metadata does not create an extra reward. Keep the candle unlit until its later canon moment.

The downstream party seam is included through the cake, table, candle, banner motifs, Rumi, Roshan sheets and two Ember cutouts. Those story characters have different visual detail from the toy jobs and need scale/value review at the seam. Their inclusion in this library grants no plot or redesign authority.

Arborist practice and the unbuilt story replacement

Tree Book practice — 4.1. The implemented optional test keeps one orange-spotted patient and asks for tree, leaf, then medicine with four choices each. It then stages approach, held treatment and healthy/sticker result. The book and full-tail Roshan are strong. Opaque navy specimen plates and similarly warm foliage/spot colors are the source weaknesses. Keep book left, patient upper right and four clear choices, while preserving patient identity through treatment.

The four spray poses are separate authored stills; a complete treatment sequence remains a runtime review. The tall pine cannot silently become the healthy version of a different broad-leaf patient. Three additional patient cases are missing. The earlier pruning/wrapping design is superseded by the owner-corrected Tree Book order.

The Sky Lagoon party-tree replacement has no built scene to score. It is explicitly listed as a gap, with a pending score, instead of inventing a successful game from the art packet. Use the existing source family when that owner-directed migration is implemented, then refresh this library against its exact build.

Evidence and limits

The 23 composition illustrations are existing September 5 captures. Each retains its source path, image hash, manifest path/hash and local evidence limit. Hall and Racer manifests name base 775ceee1 and explicitly identify diagnostic fixtures. Teacher/Geologist run01 records per-frame input origin and surface state with bounded source snapshots. These images are useful for discussing hierarchy, panel dominance and identity; they are not fresh captures of baseline 55032e88 and cannot establish current defects or fixes.

A sparse dedicated worktree was used because the available disk could not hold a full second checkout. The source census reads missing tracked images directly from the baseline Git object, preserving their bytes and hashes. It does not infer a missing runtime asset from a sparse filesystem. Official Godot 4.7.2 was used only to rasterize source SVG previews in an isolated review project. There is no new full-game import, played-state capture or local probe result claimed here.

Current visual acceptance still requires exact-build Mobile entry, accepted contact, partial, completion, repeat and return states at the required aspects; normal-speed pose/motion review; target-device readability and performance; child comprehension; and owner art acceptance. Machine checks validate coverage and source binding, not those visual claims. Existing MA-VIS-006, MA-PLAY-004 and related Opera findings retain their lifecycle and closure requirements.

Refresh this library as development changes

Use the persistent goal with: Refresh the Day Two artwork library against current origin dev and review every changed image and affected game sequence. The saved tool is a manual development trigger, not a scheduled background monitor. No unsolicited reminder schedule was created.

  1. Fetch the latest repository and use a clean codex/ task branch under the project workflow. Read the master planning entry, applicable rules, active findings and ledger again.
  2. Run python -B tools/build_day2_art_library.py --refresh. It compares the complete source census, image hashes and production-controller/shared-owner/domain-authority fingerprints. New/changed image bytes invalidate their old scores; affected composition review is marked stale. Removed files and all changed paths are written to refresh_delta.json.
  3. Visually inspect every changed image and its current composed usage. Update reviews.json with that exact source hash and an authored visual observation, draft score and next action. Re-review affected entries in evaluations.json and restore composition_status only after that review. Unchanged reviews may be retained; changed images do not inherit old acceptance or receive automatic grades.
  4. Run python -B tools/build_day2_art_library.py --render, then python -B tools/build_day2_art_library.py --check. Inspect the rendered gallery, filter counts, originals and game/phase tables. Add/update audit impact coverage, navigation and evidence before the normal gates and publication.

Keep the complete library folder together when copying or downloading it: index.html loads the local previews/ images. The packet works offline and is inspectable by the unchanged 2D audit without a large embedded-image HTML file.

The first live refresh changed exactly one inventoried file, D2A-0627 Rumi. The tool invalidated its old score before visual re-review. Its earlier hash, score and observation remain in reviews.json history. The repaired sheet still scores 4.5/5 at native size and remains a refinement priority. The associated Day Two Popstar notes were re-reviewed; unrelated pool/craft-room fixtures are not promoted into birthday acceptance.

The initial report is a dated first pass. Preserve its conclusions and evidence when beginning a later round; record revisions rather than silently rewriting earlier acceptance claims. The refresh tool identifies what needs visual review. It does not generate art, edit the game, award owner acceptance or close master findings.

Machine verification and acceptance reporting

The implementation is the illustrated source library, individual reviews, per-phase evaluations, priority CSV and refresh tool. Machine verification covers source census/hash parity, inclusive threshold, review completeness, controller/authority fingerprints, artifact rendering and repository audit gates. Exact results are recorded in the impact record and verification.log.

Current played visuals, motion/contact, device, child and owner acceptance remain outstanding. All historical captures keep their original limits. Repository probe success, when recorded at the exact published revision, is regression evidence and does not change those acceptance states.
